Adding details on rate limits, overage tiers, and an example invoice layout below. Annie — copying the language you can paste to finance.

Rate limits & burst policy (summary):
- Soft quota = monthly committed tokens. Requests above soft quota are evaluated against burst allowance.
- Burst allowance = configurable percentage above baseline (we typically set 200–300% for midsize customers during launches). Bursts are time-limited (configurable window, e.g., 2 hours) and tracked separately.
- If burst consumption remains within configured allowance and window, no penalty beyond overage unit charge. If sustained beyond allowed window, traffic is either throttled or routed to a fallback model (lower-cost variant) depending on the rollback policy.

Overage pricing model (example):
- Baseline hosted price: $X per 1M tokens (tier 1).
- Overage (hosted): 1.5x baseline per 1M tokens (applies once monthly quota exhausted).
- Dedicated reserved customers: baseline lower (Y per 1M) and overage at 1.2x baseline for ad-hoc bursts.

Sample invoice calculation (your 2-hour spike + numbers filled in):
- Baseline monthly tokens committed: 15,000,000 tokens — baseline charge: $A (15 * $/1M).
- Spike extra tokens consumed in event: 20,000,000 tokens. Overage charge (hosted): 20 * (1.5 * $/1M) = $B.
- Temporary quota increase: we can pre-authorize a one-off quota bump for X hours; billing converts that ramp to reserved price if you commit to a short-term capacity bump (~7–14 day notice preferred for large sustained increases).

Operational: temporary quota increases go through our support ops queue; approvals: CSM/AE + finance contact (email ok). For emergency one-off bursts we can escalate to infra on-call for a manual bump; SLA to respond is 2 business hours for high-priority escalations (we recommend pre-authorized windows for launches).

Attached: SOW-draft.pdf with a placeholder priced for a 3-month evaluation + optional dedicated pool trial.

Let us know your preferred target $/1M and I’ll run a quick table with what that means to your monthly/overage costs.

—Ben
